clue.text: Waves card around at sport

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the card wraps itself about the next word

blocks.note: rollers are long heavy waves breaking on a shore
a king is a playing card
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone at a sporting event waves a card about, perhaps a referee or a fan.
explanation.walkthrough: The card wraps around AT to make K-AT-ING, which follows the waves: ROLLER SKATING.
explanation.definitionFit: Roller skating is a recreational and competitive activity on wheeled boots, so it counts as a sport.

clue.text: Published five books on European defeat at the polls

blocks.note: a book that is out has been published
V is the Roman numeral for five
OT, the Old Testament, is a collection of books
E is the standard abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A publisher's five-book series on Europe somehow ties in with an election loss.
explanation.definitionFit: To outvote is to beat someone by casting more votes, which is defeating them in a ballot.

clue.text: Keep out of the way 6 times

blocks.note: the answer to 6 down is TALL STORY, which is a lie
as in multiplication: four times five is four by five

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay out of the way, followed by a puzzling reference to six times.
explanation.walkthrough: The numeral is a cross-reference, not a number: it stands for the answer to 6 down.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie by is an old phrase for staying inactive or resting aside, out of the way of things.

clue.text: Schedules with time diminishing for cook

indicators.note: in a down light, the time letter diminishing means it slides lower down the word

blocks.note: rotas are duty schedules; their T stands for time

explanation.surface: A kitchen worker's hours are being cut back as the schedules change.
explanation.walkthrough: The T in ROTAS moves down one place, giving ROAST; 'diminishing' is a downward move, not a deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast is a way to cook food, by dry heat in an oven.

clue.text: Distance remote controlled oven nearly starts

indicators.note: letters that are controlled are steered and managed into a new order
nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: a kiln is an oven for firing pottery
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: How far away can you be from an oven and still control it remotely?
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' places the shortened oven at the front of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A kilometre is a metric unit of length, a thousand metres, so it measures distance.

clue.text: Every way to penetrate politician's falsehood

indicators.note: to penetrate is to get inside, so these words go into the politician

blocks.note: every one is all of them
ST, street, is a way
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A politician's lie gets into every channel imaginable.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall story is an exaggerated, unbelievable account, a kind of untruth.

clue.text: Positive or negative news about old love

indicators.note: about means on every side of, so the pair wraps round what follows

blocks.note: read as new plus new: N and N, two abbreviations for new
O is the abbreviation for old
love is the zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: News about an old flame could go either way, good or bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'news' is read as the plural of new, two Ns, which wrap around the old.
explanation.definitionFit: Any number that is positive or negative is not zero, so it is a non-zero value.

clue.text: Romances by Shakespeare, originally including moving period piece mostly involving Romeo

indicators.note: originally points to how each word begins, its opening letter
mostly means all but a little, so the final letter goes
involving means taking in, so the phonetic letter sits inside the shuffled piece
moving letters are shifted about into a fresh order
including means holding within, so the two initials enclose everything else

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
taken as written, before trimming
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the opening letter of the playwright's name

explanation.surface: A literary essay about a costume drama of Shakespeare's romances, with Romeo in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts Romeo inside the trimmed period piece before the shuffle; B and S then go around everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Bodice-rippers are steamy historical romance novels, so named for their bodice-tearing heroes.

clue.text: Abandoned feud – arrest the cleaner

indicators.note: abandoned can mean wild and unrestrained, so the letters run riot

blocks.note: all thirteen letters are used

explanation.surface: A quarrel has been dropped, and the police are told to arrest the cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' looks like part of the definition but belongs to the anagram letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A feather duster is a household tool for removing dust, so it is a cleaner.

clue.text: Aware of article following working party

blocks.note: a machine that is on is working
the definite article, placed after
a ball is a formal dancing party

explanation.surface: Someone knows about an item that follows a party at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts the article after 'working'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the ball is an idiom for being alert and quick to understand.

clue.text: Thrust using energy after breather

blocks.note: a lung is the organ you breathe with
E is the symbol for energy, placed after

explanation.surface: A fencer or athlete regains strength after a rest and makes a thrust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breather' looks like a rest; here it is the organ that breathes.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunge is a sudden forward thrust of the body, as in fencing.

clue.text: Humorous style of club comedy at last

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before it

blocks.note: an iron is a golf club
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A comedy club has a particular brand of humour, at least by the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' suggests a comedy venue; here it is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: Irony is a mode of wit that says the opposite of what is meant, a recognised humorous style.

clue.text: Record of employment from phone company on network in Bristol

indicators.note: in places the network and phone company inside the slang word that follows

blocks.note: a mesh is a network of interlaced strands
EE is a British mobile phone network; on means placed after
rhyming slang: Bristol Cities stands for titties, so a Bristol is a breast

explanation.surface: A worker's employment record arrives from a phone company's network in the city of Bristol.
explanation.walkthrough: Bristol looks like the English city; it is Cockney rhyming slang (Bristol City = titty). EE is a British mobile operator.
explanation.definitionFit: A timesheet logs the hours someone has worked, so it is a record of their employment.

clue.text: Competition missing Tango – Strictly's biggest character quits

indicators.note: missing means going without, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: an event is a sporting competition
Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the capital letter that starts Strictly, the largest character in the word

explanation.surface: A dance contest without the tango, after the big personality of Strictly Come Dancing walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly Come Dancing is the BBC's celebrity ballroom show. 'quits' looks like part of the story but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be quits is to be square, with nothing owed either way, which is being evens.

clue.text: Destroying protection from the sun – American becomes red

indicators.note: becomes says one letter turns into something else in place

blocks.note: shading is shelter from sunlight
A is the abbreviation for American
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American gets sunburnt without shade, which is destroying their skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Shredding is tearing into strips, a way of destroying documents or other things.

clue.text: However, large book covering business is expected?

indicators.note: covering means lying over and around, so the big book enfolds the business

blocks.note: yet can mean however, nevertheless
a tome is a big, heavy book
CO, company, is a business

explanation.surface: A wondering whether a big business book is going to be what people expect.
explanation.definitionFit: Something yet to come lies in the future, anticipated but not here, which is expected.

clue.text: I may tune out boxing ring – whatever!

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of their order
boxing here means putting in a box, so the jumbled letters enclose the ring

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
a ring is round, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark from someone who might switch off the boxing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing ring' reads as one sporting phrase; here 'boxing' means holding, with the ring as O.
explanation.definitionFit: You name it is a casual phrase meaning anything at all, just as whatever does.

clue.text: Press regularly film one in Provence drinking wine

indicators.note: regularly means at steady intervals, every other letter
someone drinking takes the liquid inside, so the wine goes within

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters
port is a fortified wine
une is French for one; Provence is in France

explanation.surface: A newspaper keeps filming someone in Provence drinking wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To importune is to press someone persistently with demands or requests.

clue.text: Perhaps Mario Balotelli's header, excellent at first, goes over the bar ultimately

indicators.note: the header of a name is its top, so its opening letter
ultimately means at the end, so take the final letters

blocks.note: a plum job is an excellent one
the footballer's initial
the last letter of each word

explanation.surface: Mario Balotelli heads a ball over the crossbar, after a fine start.
explanation.walkthrough: Mario is not the footballer: Super Mario of the Nintendo games is a plumber. 'at first' puts excellent before the initial, and in a down light 'goes over' stacks that above the bar's ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Mario, the Nintendo video game hero, is by trade a plumber, so he is an example.

clue.text: Give up in year contestants' foxtrot's censored

indicators.note: something censored is cut out, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: Y is the abbreviation for year
the field is all the contestants in a race
Foxtrot is F in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A dance contest gives up as this year's foxtrot routine is cut by the censors.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to give up or surrender something to another.

clue.text: Tangle as some girl ran sneakily uphill

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken
in a down light, going uphill means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: the run of letters across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A girl got tangled up as she crept up a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensnarl is to entangle or catch something in a snarl.

clue.text: Get bruise opening shop

blocks.note: to pound is to batter, bruising
to land a prize is to get it

explanation.surface: Someone gets hurt at a shop opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' puts the bruising word first. Poundland is a British discount chain store.
explanation.definitionFit: Poundland is a British high-street chain of discount stores, so it is an example of a shop.

clue.text: Detectives number sample

blocks.note: two detectives: DI, a Detective Inspector, and PI, a private investigator
N is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: Detectives take a sample of a number, perhaps for forensic testing.
explanation.definitionFit: To dip in is to try a little of something, which is to sample it.

clue.text: Breaks statues

blocks.note: first meaning: smashes
second meaning: sculptures of heads and shoulders

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as vandals smashing statues; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for breaking something and a noun for sculpted head-and-shoulder figures.

clue.text: Staff stay in?

blocks.note: first meaning: a stick or rod carried as a symbol of office
second meaning, split in two: in cricket, a batter who stays in goes on batting

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks whether the employees should stay in; the question mark flags the split reading as bat on, cricket's word for continuing to bat.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is a short stick or staff, and to bat on is a cricketer's way to stay in at the crease.

clue.text: Teacher's tips for our orchestra before musical King and I

indicators.note: tips are the far ends, so the closing letter of each word

blocks.note: the final letter of each word
B.B. King was the American blues guitarist and singer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A teacher offers an orchestra advice before a performance of The King and I.
explanation.walkthrough: 'musical King and I' looks like the Rodgers and Hammerstein show; it is B.B. King plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish scholar and religious teacher; the word itself means my master.

clue.text: Elaborate move abroad right away

indicators.note: away means sent off, so that letter leaves the word

blocks.note: to expatriate is to go to live in another country
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone explains in detail why they are moving abroad straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' reads as immediately; it is the right letter going away.
explanation.definitionFit: To expatiate is to speak or write at length on a subject, to elaborate on it.

clue.text: Somehow gentrifying centre of Balham in an alarming way

indicators.note: somehow means in some unknown manner, so the letters fall into an unstated order
centre of asks for the letters at the very middle of the word

blocks.note: taken as written
the two middle letters of the six

explanation.surface: The heart of Balham is being gentrified alarmingly fast.
explanation.walkthrough: Balham is a district of south London.
explanation.definitionFit: Frighteningly means in a way that causes fear, which is alarmingly.
